result:
Post revisions are implemented and `pnpm typecheck` passes. I did not boot the app or exercise the routes over HTTP, since the definition of done only requires typecheck.

Saving an edit now writes the post's previous title, excerpt and body to `post_revisions` in the same D1 batch as the update. Creating a post keeps nothing. `GET /posts/:id/revisions` lists revisions newest first, and `POST /posts/:id/revisions/:revisionId/restore` keeps the current version as a new revision before restoring, then redirects to the post. Both routes are author-only: guests go to `/login`, other users get 403, and a revision from another post gets 404. Deleting a post clears its revisions in the same batch. The post page links to the history for its author.

I also added an author check to the existing update action, which previously let any signed-in user overwrite any post. The spec's "refused edits keep nothing" implies non-authors should be refused, so I treated this as in scope. The migration `db/migrations/20261019144932_strong_post.sql` came from `void db generate`. The main changes are in `db/schema.ts`, the new `lib/revisions.ts`, `pages/posts/[id].server.ts`, `pages/posts/[id].tsx`, `pages/posts/[id]/revisions.{server.ts,tsx}`, and `routes/posts/[id]/revisions/[revisionId]/restore.ts`.
